cases.derivation: From test_normalize_review.test_review_code_composition_parses_with_relative_paths_and_stamps_timing, without the clock-dependent stamp, which cargo tests pin with a fixed clock. Findings, then questions, then observations become items in that order; an absolute anchor under --clone becomes repository-relative and a relative one is kept; a claim is '<title>. <trigger>' stripped, so a missing trigger leaves 'Untitled trigger.'. The document starts with arm and is json.dumps(indent=2) with a final newline.

From test_normalize_review.test_review_code_without_a_status_is_unresolved_and_not_stamped. The unresolved document is still written, the one stdout line follows, the exit is 1 and timing.json keeps its bytes.
From test_normalize_review.test_builtin_empty_array_is_an_empty_review: a fenced empty array is the verdict empty-array and parse status empty.
From test_normalize_review.test_builtin_prose_without_markers_is_unresolved_and_kept_raw. The stripped final text is one item, there is no verdict or source, and timing.json is not stamped.

From test_normalize_review.test_builtin_fenced_json_with_an_unescaped_quote_is_unresolved_and_kept_whole (2026-10-08-last-push-claude-fable att-012). The bare quote ends the second failure_scenario string, so json.loads stops at the next character with JSONDecodeError.msg "Expecting ',' delimiter"; the note carries only that message, and the whole bracketed text is one item.
From the same test with the quote escaped: both findings parse, line fills line_start and line_end, summary is the claim and failure_scenario the consequence.
From test_normalize_review.test_builtin_report_findings_calls_from_several_workers_are_all_kept: every call's findings are items in call order, and verdict fills native_confidence.

From test_normalize_review.test_codex_verdict_comes_from_the_rollout_when_given, with a second rollout. Rollouts are read in sorted(Path.rglob()) order, which compares path components: sessions/2026/01/01 sorts before sessions/2026/01-01 because '01' < '01-01', though '-' sorts before '/' in the whole path. The last value found wins, escaped inside a JSON string or bare, so the verdict is 'patch is correct'.
From test_normalize_review.test_codex_output_in_an_unknown_form_is_unresolved. Without a marker every line is summary, joined by spaces as the verdict, and the stripped stdout is kept as one item.

From normalize_review.py --self-test: Codex prints only its summary when it reports nothing, and that is empty only when the rollout's verdict is 'patch is correct'. The rollout's last line has no newline.

CRLF stdout is read with universal newlines. Indented lines extend the current item's consequence, including a raw item's. A '* [P1]' bullet does not match '- [P<n>]', so it is kept raw with a note and the result is unresolved. An end line defaults to the start line. Non-ASCII text is escaped as json.dumps escapes it.

From test_normalize_review.test_codex_skill_preserves_native_report_and_normalizes_primary_findings_once. Only findings become items; each keeps its whole source object as native_fields, after kind, and the whole report is native_payload.
From test_normalize_review.test_codex_skill_complete_empty_report_is_empty.

From test_normalize_review.test_codex_skill_incomplete_report_is_unresolved_but_keeps_items, on the claude-skill arm. A finding without a title is claimed by its json.dumps(ensure_ascii=False); line 0 is not positive, so it is null. Notes follow the finding checks, then the status (quoted with repr), then the verdict; without a text verdict the status is the native verdict.
A report that is not an object is kept whole: its json.dumps(ensure_ascii=False) is the one claim and it is native_payload; the output then escapes the non-ASCII character.
From test_normalize_review.test_unreadable_input_exits_2_and_writes_nothing: str(JSONDecodeError) after the program name, exit 2, and no output file.
From the same test: the OSError quotes the path as given, unnormalized.
From test_normalize_review.test_an_unreadable_timing_sidecar_exits_2. The result is written before the sidecar is read, so normalized.json exists and timing.json keeps its bytes.
Opening a directory for reading fails with EISDIR, which is caught and reported as OSError.
print(text) writes the document and its newline, then the unresolved line.
Integers keep every digit, 1.5E0 is written as float.__repr__ spells it, and NaN is written NaN.
A repeated key keeps its last value. The claim formats each value as an f-string does: a dict by repr with Python's True and None. The missing anchor path defaults to the empty text.

From test_normalize_review.test_render_strips_priority_and_verdict. Items are joined by a blank line and print adds the last newline; a missing file is '(no file)', a range shows its end only when it differs, and an empty consequence or fix is an em dash.
From the same test: an empty list renders '(no items)'.

CODEX_BULLET's \d is a str pattern, so it matches every Unicode decimal digit (category Nd), and int() reads their values: P١ is the priority and ١٢-١٣ is lines 12 to 13. native_priority keeps the matched text, which json.dumps escapes.
open(encoding='utf-8') raises UnicodeDecodeError, which main does not catch. The port reports the codec error after the path and writes nothing.
Iterating an integer findings value raises TypeError in from_review_code, which main does not catch. The port names the field and writes nothing.
Opening a directory for writing raises IsADirectoryError outside main's try block. The port reports str(OSError) after the program name, as the input errors do.
Assigning payload_validated_at into a list raises TypeError, which the timing block does not catch. The result is already written and the sidecar keeps its bytes in both.
json.loads raises ValueError for an integer of more than 4300 digits, which is not the JSONDecodeError from_claude_builtin catches. The port reports Python's limit message and writes nothing.

U+116D1 MYANMAR PAO DIGIT ONE and U+10D41-U+10D42 GARAY DIGIT ONE and TWO are category Nd from Unicode 16.0, so Python 3.14's \d matches them: the priority is P plus U+116D1, which json.dumps escapes as a surrogate pair, and the bullet is line 12. An interpreter with an older database does not match the bullet and keeps the line raw, with the indented body as its consequence.
